The point

The lowest-friction route is not always the cheapest.

The index values action count, wallet interruption, and uncertainty alongside price.

Median user burden —

clicks + wallet prompts in this scenario

Approval tax —

routes that asked for a token approval

A repeatable project, not a claim of universal truth

Run the same test. Publish the trade-offs.

  1. Standardize. Fix token, amount, source, destination, wallet, and starting balance.
  2. Observe. Count explicit clicks, wallet prompts, approvals, and network changes.
  3. Time. Start at route selection; stop when funds are spendable on the destination.
  4. Repeat. Log timestamp and quote; route availability and fees change constantly.

How the friction index works

The score makes invisible interaction cost comparable. It is a research heuristic, not a safety or quality rating.

clicks × 1wallet prompts × 2approvals × 3network switches × 2+ latency minutes ÷ 5

Use the same protocol and weighting for every route. If your users care more about a specific burden, adapt the weights and disclose the change.
